From: W.A. Yates, CHORLEY




Dear Brian,

I am delighted with the final
alterations to the folio program
- it really is an enormous succ-
ess. I have now given it a comp-
lete trial in TAPE, MICRO-DRIVE
and DISC versions and the DISC
version is as superior to be al-
most beyond belief.

Loading,  entering,  updating,
saving and printing was a slow
and tedious task with the TAPE
version and not averse to crash-
ing.


MICRODRIVE just flirts and teas-
es and plays with one's emotions
until you feel that you are
about to succeed- at which point
it crashes all your desires to
the ground (does that bring back
memories?).[sure does! - Ed]

DISC is marvellous; it does it
all so easily and so satisfact-
orily. It really enjoys load and
reload, GO TO and makes it so
much easier to correct mistakes.

I am very appreciative of your
efforts, whilst P.D., it may be,
if there was any justice, you
should be able to claim copy-
right under the title of"Brian's
program coat of many patches".
Thank you.


BRIAN AND CHRIS,I am very grate-
ful for your help with Chess-
board following your comment and
advice I retyped it and it load-
ed and ran correctly first time!

I had actually picked up the
comma in DATA Line 50 and the
capital 'I', but unfortunately
sent the wrong copy to you (NOTE
I must always check the copies
as well as the entry lines).


Line 70 I left spaces before and
after.  I doubt if it would ever
have ocurred to me to use white
squares(that's good information)
and I was struggling on the
Graphics and have learned from
your comments.


Thank you once again.  I still
have no idea how the chessmen
take their shape. I realize that
it has to be by the DATA numbers
but can you please point me in
the right directon?

     Yours very sincerely,

          W.A. Yates

Brian Cavers to Arnold Yates

We've an even better chessboard
routine in the pipeline which
should be in OUTLET soon. Watch
out for it!

User-defined graphics(UDGs),like
all images on a Spectrum screen,
including text, are made up of
tiny dots. 8 of these dots are
stored in each byte of computer
screen memory. A byte is a value
from 0 to 255. The computer
represents each byte by using 8
'bits', each of which can be one
or zero. There are 256 combinat-
ions of 8 ones or zeros, eg,
11001100, 11000000, 00011100.
Those 256 combinations gives the
values 0 to 255...


Representing values in this way
is called binary representation,
as distinct from decimal which
we we normally (humanly) use,eg,
a column for thousands,hundreds,
tens and units. For example, the
value 204 is binary 11001100.You
can prove this by typing...
      PRINT BIN 11001100

Imagine a chess piece (or any
other image) made up of these 1s
and 0s...
          00000000 =   0
          00111000 =  56
          00111000 =  56
          01111100 = 124
          00111000 =  56
          00111000 =  56
          01111100 = 124
          11111110 = 254


If you store those values in a
BASIC DATA statement...

9500 DATA 0, 56, 56, 124, 56, 56
          ,124, 254
                 ...like in that
chessboard program and POKE them
into the udg area as shown in
the program. You can then print
the UDG and it will display the
image,eg...
9300 RESTORE 9500
9400 FOR A=USR "A" TO USR "A"+7
     READ B : POKE A,B : NEXT A
9500 PRINT "A"

In line 9500 you must press the
graphics key before and after
typing the "A" but in line 9400
you can use EITHER a normal "A"
OR a graphic "A".


I might add that the 'USR' in
the program is the Spectrum's
way (used in that form) of find-
ing the right place in memory
for each UDG from A to S (A to U
in 48K).

There are programs to help you
create these udgs which can be
saved and loaded as code without
those pokes. There was a very
good one in OUTLET 78 called
GRAPHIX. However, in the coming
new chessboard program, Francis
Miles shows a simple way to do
it from BASIC using BIN (more or
less the same way I do it myself
for odds and ends).

I hope that clarifies how UDGs
are formed but let me know if
you want more!             Brian

From H. Smart, SELKIRK

Dear Ron,

A while ago I wrote asking your
advice about my problems with my
two computers - a Plus 2A and a
Plus 2. I have had the Plus 2A
for a few years and wanted a
disk drive for it. I managed to
get one secondhand and with a
Plus 2. However, I could not get
the disk drive to work with the
Plus 2A and you suggested I get
a "widget" from Datel. This I
did but it will only work in 48K
mode. If I try to get it to work
in 128K mode it resets the comp-
uter to 48K mode!1 I hve written
to Datel but have yet to receive
a reply.


I also can't get the printer (a
Newbury Data 1500 made by C.Itoh
Inc.) to work with the Plus 2.

It works fine with the Plus 2A
as you can see by this letter
but I can only use it from tape.
I enter BASIC and enter: LINE 60
FORMAT LINE 2400: FORMAT LPRINT
"R" : FORMAT LPRINT "U" as per
the manual and it works OK.

With the Plus 2 I go into BASIC
and enter RANDOMIZE USR 40458 :
FORMAT "P";2400 (2400 is the
baud rate of the printer) but
all I get from the printer is
garbage!

I wrote to Tasman but they said
they can't help me.
                       H. Smart

Brian Cavers to H. Smart


You also mentioned previously
that the +D obscured the RS232
socket - though you may be int-
erested in Les Tyler's OUTLETTER
this month on that topic.

Thus to summarise...


A. The PLUS 2 works OK with the
   Plus D but the printer prints
   garbage and also cannot be
   connected with the Plus D.

B. The PLUS 2A works OK with the
   printer but only in 48K with
   the Plus D.



1. Did you get the correct
   "widget" from Datel? Did
   you tell them EXACTLY which
   Spectrum it was for when you
   ordered it?

2. Try the Plus 2 WITHOUT the +D
   with the printer FROM BASIC
   using the standard syntax and
   then just LPRINT "TESTING".Do
   you know the correct syntax
   to initialize a printer from
   the Plus 2? I regret I do not
   have the manual. I don't know
   if FORMAT "P";2400 is the
   whole story. Can anyone else
   confirm this. Is there an
   equivalent to the +2A/+3's
   FORMAT LPRINT "R" to initial-
   ize RS232 printing or is that
   set up by default?


If you can get the Plus 2 to run
OK from BASIC then that points
to the problem being in Tasword
Plus 2. I do not have the Tas+2
manual. What does it say is the
purpose of the USR 40458?

Have you got the +D configured
correctly? You need to have DOS
set for serial printing. If
unsure, use POKE @ 11,1. If this
gets it to work then you could
resave DOS to save having to do
the POKE @ every time you boot
up DOS.

Has anyone else any suggestions?

                       Brian

From Les Tyler, CHELTENHAM

In response to the reader
[H.Smart] who is having problems
with the RS232 socket on his +2
when using the +D - this has
always been a bit of a problem
with me too,especially as I also
use the socket for MIDI purposes
driving a keyboard.  In actual
fact,though,it is no great diff-
iculty, as it IS possible to use
the socket with a +D plugged in,
albeit with a little 'fiddling'.

If you first plug in the printer
or what-have-you and then GENTLY
hold the BT plug up with your
fingers,at the same time sliding
the +D connector on it should go
on OK: rather a tight fit but it
will go.

If the space is still too tight,
try shaving a very thin slice
off the printer plug's plastic
case.  I found I had to do this
with the standard BT plug on a
MIDI lead but when I bought a
made-up lead for my printer I
found it was not necessary -
simply a case of variation in
size, I guess.

A possibly useful tip,try loose-
ning the screws holding the base
of the computer, this might give
you sufficient room at the edge
connector to slide on the +D.

Nowadays I can plug in either
the printer or keyboard together
with the +D and there is little
or no problem. I hope this is of
assistance !

As you observed in your reply to
the original letter on this sub-
ject, there should be no problem
with the +2a using Brian Gaff's
'thingy', as this should keep
the +D well clear of the +2a's
casing, giving sufficient room
for the BT plug.

                 Les Tyler

From:Sam Quigg, LIMAVADY

Dear Ron & Brian,

I have just received my second
issue of OUTLET. I am delighted
with the product, with its pres-
entation, content and relevance
to the consumer.

I am a relatively new member of
the Spectrum fraternity, having
purchased a grey +2 some ten
months ago to produce video
titles. I now have in addition a
48k (rubber keys) and a 128+3.
My most recent acquisition has
been a +D interface and twin DD
drives. I print via an Epson
FX-80 printer,or via an Alphacom
32 (kindly donated by a friend.)


I find that the + 3 will not run
with the +D interface, even with
the recommended FIXER board in-
stalled.

The system disk I am using to
boot the +3 was produced on the
+2, as the TAPE/SOUND socket on
the +3 is defunct. Could this be
the problem?

            Regards,

                 Sam Quigg

 P.S. I still don't have any
      video titles!!!

Brian Cavers to Sam Quigg

I still have my old Alphacom in
the cupboard. It was always much
more handy for printing out a
few lines of calculations or to
dump some text off the screen.My
current Epson wastes a sheet of
A4 for every little thing I want
to print. It also likes to screw
up the paper now and again and,
although giving better quality
for letters,etc, is nowhere near
so handy.

I can't remember if I've ever
tried it in tandem with the +D.
I've got the idea it wouldn't
work but I'm beginning to wonder
now. POKE @11, 0 or 1 should
switch between +D and ZX prints.
Maybe I'll give it a try.

If the 'FIXER' you refer to is
the 'FIXIT' from BG SERVICES, it
should work. Maybe it's provided
by Datel but I imagine it's the
same sort of thing. To use the
+D from 128K BASIC I understand
you need to boot the +D system
file (presumably in 48K mode)
and then do...

 POKE @4426,16 : POKE @4427,92

If you then reset the Spectrum,
the +D should work from 128K
BASIC. You should then be able
to re-save the DOS with...

SAVE d1;"+SYS 2a" CODE 8192,6656

Substitute whatever DOS name you
have already but KEEP YOUR ORIG-
INAL ON ANOTHER DISK.

I don't know if you can then use
the +D normally but perhaps some
other reader can write in to say
what other peculiarities there
are with this setup. I do know
that many people are using it
quite happily so it must be pos-
sible.
                        Brian

From: Bill Buxton, CHESHIRE





Dear Brian,

Regarding my recent query of the
possibility of connecting a +3
with a TA mono monitor via the
RGB/PERITEL socket, the follow-
ing may be of interest to OUTLET
readers.

As suggested by yourselves, I
contacted Meedmore Ltd,  of 28
Farriers Way Industrial Estate,
netherton, Merseyside, L30 4XL
(Tel: 0151 521 2202)  and they
informed me as follows...


"Unfortunately, you will not be
able to use the VGA monitor with
your computer. The problem is
that the Spectrum works at a
frequency of 15.75 MHz and the
monitor (VGA) needs a frequency
of 30Mhz to be able to get a
picture. I would advise you to
look for a Phillips CM8833 or
one of the CBM1084 range of mon-
itors if you wish to use RGB."

They also sent me a very inform-
ative catalogue which lists the
necessary cable leads required
and suppplied by them to connect
a large range of computers to
compatible monitors. An SAE to
this company will be well worth-
while for OUTLET readers who may
be considering upgrading their


equipment to include a monitor
in lieu of or as well as an ord-
inary tv set.

I very much appreciate your help
in this matter.

       Yours faithfully,

          Bill Buxton



Brian Cavers to Bill Buxton



Thanks Bill.You may also be int-
erested to read Malcolm Perry's
letter this month on this topic
although I do not now know if it
will help if what Meedmore says
is true.


Looking back at your original
letter in last month's OUTLET, I
see that you do not actually say
that your monitor is VGA. Indeed
you say it is monochrome.I don't
know for sure but think that VGA
is always colour.Most modern PCs
are VGA or SVGA so Meedmore may
have assumed yours was.


However, I'm sure you must have
told Meedmore that it was a mono
monitor and they know what they
are talking about. If not, poss-
ibly Malcolm's info might be of
use after all?

                         Brian

From:Malcolm Perry,KIDDERMINSTER


Dear Brian.

Re:Mr Buxton's request for conn-
ecting a mono monitor to the +3,
unfortunately I have not come
across this actual model and the
info is lacking in some essen-
tial details. I do not have or
any info on PC technicalities so
the following is only guesswork.

Assuming the monitor is compat-
ible with the TV standard used
on the Spectrum the info given
does not give video and sync
levels so I will assume they are
the norm of around 1V video and
3 to 4V TTL sync.


The main problem is that the +3
does not provide any mono video
only the SCART/RGB + SYNC.  Now,
if used solely for word process-
ing, it would be possible to set
paper and ink colours such that
a single connection from any one
of R, G or B would give a satis-
factory display.However,for gen-
eral use this would be totally
unsatisfactory.

Simply combining R, G and B to a
single video output would be
unsatisfactory as all colours
being at the same level would
merge into one another and at
times lose information in a gen-
eral black/white "splodge ":like
the problems with +D printouts
on some colour combinations.


In practice,R,G & B are combined
at different levels so as to
produce a grey scale and so re-
tain definition over the screen
from each colour. I have tried
the following on a 128 and it
worked fine into a mono monitor
providing a grey scale. It could
be done with resistors of diff-
erent values...

R------>------:
        D     :
              :
G-------------:------- mono out
              :
      D D     :  D= 1N914 diode
B------>->----:     or similar

                 --->---
                 -     +
                    (marked end)

The next problem is that the
computer outputs combined H & V
sync while the monitor requires
them separately. Depending on
the internal circuits of the
sync inputs it may work simply
by joining them together and
connecting to the Spectrum sync.
output. However it may need a
resistor or diode in series with
one or the other or both to give
required results.


I would guess the "reserved"
connections are either used to
tell the PC what type of monitor
is connected or they relate to
pins used for the additional
signals ie, RGB for colour mon-
itors.


While there is a fair chance of
obtaining a satisfactory outcome
on my part, it would be by trial
and error.  This is a bit risky
to put to others because if by
trial I get an error and cause
damage to my own computer or
monitor, that is my own fault.
Offering an unproved suggestion
to others and have them damage
items is a different matter. So,
as Brian suggested in such as
this case, perhaps it is better
to ask a firm that no doubt has
more and full details of the
actual monitor being connected.


But if a reader wants to take a
risk the information would
indicate...


Derived video from Spectrum as
above to pin 2.
Spec. sync pin 4 to pins 13 & 14
Spec GND pin 2 to pin 10

If this does not produce a dis-
play of some sorts then Video
return pin 7 would indicate a
separate video GND so connect to
pin 10 - probably kept separate
on the PC to reduce interference
on the video signal...
SPECTRUM      MONITOR
7  R-
6  G- ]--------- 2
8  B-

4  Syn--------:- 13
              :- 14

2  GND--------:- 10
              :- 7.

           John Hall
       16 Singleton Drive
          Ensbury Park
          Bournemouth
             Dorset
            BH10 4BT




Dear Ron & Brian,

For over a year now I have been
using an Amiga A1200 instead of
the Spectrum. My main interest
is producing films from my cam-
corder,editing them on the Amiga
and producing titles for them
and, as you no doubt know, this
is far easier on the Amiga than
on the Spectrum.


Whilst I am sorting out my Spec-
trum bits and pieces I don't
know whether you or maybe a
fellow user would be interested
but I have a series of articles
saved from Everyday Electronics
entitled "On Spec". These were
written by Mike Toooley B.A. and
are mainly circuits to construct
add-ons for the various Spectrum
computers. They date from April
1985 until the series closed in
October, 1990.

I've also two sets of magazines,
one called "Input" which covers
Spectrum, Commodore 64, Acorn
Electron & BBC, Dragon 32, ZX81,
Vic 20, Tandy TRS80. These are
filled with programs to type in
for the various machines. there
is virtually a complete set.

The other one is called"The Home
Computer Course". The content is
obvious with a large amount of
space directed to the Spectrum;
again, almost a complete set.

I would hate to see these items
end up in the bin. All I ask is
adequate postage if anyone is
interested. I have various other
hardware and software bits and
pieces too.

Best wishes for the future,

           John Hall

Brian Cavers to John Hall

Thanks, John.

Any readers interested in any of
the items John has on offer,will
you please write direct to the
address at the top of John's
letter.

                      Brian

         ANDREW FLEMING
        64 FEROZESHAH RD
       DEVIZES, WILTSHIRE
            SN10 2JH

          01380-725111

I unearthed my system a few days
ago, not really expecting it to
work after 3 years buried in a
corner. Surprise for ME! it pow-
ered up and went to work as if
nothing had happened.  The only
problem was me: I had forgotten
a lot.

OOps,There was a bit of a hiccup
here.I had to switch off and put
the coffee on because I had a
visitor. I came back an hour or
so later and the drives refused
to power up.

I can't blame them:they've had a
hammering these last few days in
10 to 12 hours a session running
through a lot of my old OUTLETS.

My drives are dual 3.5"s in a
black box, purchased from MGT in
their heyday eight or nine years
ago. As neither drive would go,
I suspected the transformer had
gone but there was no smell of
burnt insulation.

I had a friend run over it with
an AVO but could find nothing
wrong. I concluded that as the
drives and other bits are all
totally enclosed in a heavy
metal case with no vents, the
transformer had overheated and
triggered a thermister which had
reset on cooling.

The case now has vents which I
hope will prevent a recurrence.

I have spent a few days going
through all 76 of my OUTLET
discs and it was only when I got
to the last three or four that I
realised that I had never had
the opportunity to look at them
when I received them. They are
all as brilliant as I remembered
- and there was mention of a +D
CATLOADER so good it has to be
sold as a separate program. I
would like one please!

In case you have discarded all
record of me, a reminder of my
system... Grey +2,+D, the afore-
mentioned double disc drives,and
Sony tv/monitor.
                   Andy Fleming

Brian Cavers to Andrew Fleming

No, we don't forget our old cus-
tomers and you should by now
have received a copy of the our
CATLOADER - the best front-end
file-handler for any Spectrum
drive system!

                          Brian.

У нас на подходе еще более удачная подпрограмма шахматной доски, которая скоро появится в OUTLET. Следите за выпусками!

Пользовательские символы (UDG), как и любые изображения на экране Spectrum (включая текст), состоят из крошечных точек. 8 таких точек хранятся в каждом байте экранной памяти компьютера. Байт — это значение от 0 до 255. Компьютер представляет каждый байт с помощью 8 «битов», каждый из которых может быть единицей или нулем. Существует 256 комбинаций из 8 единиц или нулей, например: 11001100, 11000000, 00011100. Эти 256 комбинаций и дают значения от 0 до 255...

Представление значений таким способом называется двоичным представлением, в отличие от десятичного, которое мы обычно используем (в человеческой жизни), например, столбцы для тысяч, сотен, десятков и единиц. Например, значение 204 в двоичной системе равно 11001100. Вы можете проверить это, набрав:

```text
PRINT BIN 11001100
```

Представьте себе шахматную фигуру (или любое другое изображение), составленную из этих единиц и нулей...

```text
00000000 =   0
00111000 =  56
00111000 =  56
01111100 = 124
00111000 =  56
00111000 =  56
01111100 = 124
11111110 = 254
```

Если вы сохраните эти значения в операторе Бейсика DATA...

```text
9500 DATA 0, 56, 56, 124, 56, 56, 124, 254
```

...как в той программе с шахматной доской, и занесете их с помощью POKE в область UDG, как показано в программе. После этого вы сможете напечатать UDG, и на экране появится изображение, например:

```text
9300 RESTORE 9500
9400 FOR A=USR "A" TO USR "A"+7
     READ B : POKE A,B : NEXT A
9500 PRINT "A"
```

В строке 9500 вы должны нажать клавишу графики до и после ввода «A», но в строке 9400 вы можете использовать ЛИБО обычную «A», ЛИБО графическую «A».

Добавлю, что 'USR' в программе — это способ Spectrum (при использовании в такой форме) находить нужное место в памяти для каждого UDG от A до S (от A до U в 48K).

Существуют программы, помогающие создавать эти UDG, которые затем можно сохранять и загружать в виде машинного кода без всяких POKE. Очень хорошая программа была в OUTLET 78 под названием GRAPHIX. Однако в грядущей новой шахматной программе Francis Miles покажет простой способ сделать это из Бейсика с помощью BIN (примерно так же, как я сам делаю для всяких мелочей).

Надеюсь, это прояснило, как формируются UDG, но дайте знать, если вам нужны подробности!

Главная проблема в том, что +3 не выдаёт монохромного видеосигнала — только SCART/RGB + SYNC. Если использовать компьютер исключительно для текстового редактора, можно было бы подобрать цвета paper и ink так, чтобы одиночный провод от любого из сигналов R, G или B давал приемлемую картинку. Однако для общего применения это совершенно не годится.

Простое объединение R, G и B в один видеовыход тоже не подойдёт, так как все цвета, находясь на одном уровне, сольются друг с другом, и временами информация будет теряться в общем чёрно-белом пятне — наподобие проблем с распечатками на +D при некоторых цветовых комбинациях.

На практике R, G и B объединяются с разными уровнями, чтобы получить шкалу серого и тем самым сохранить чёткость каждого цвета на экране. Я пробовал следующий вариант на 128-м, и он отлично работал с монохромным монитором, формируя градации серого. Это можно сделать с помощью резисторов разного номинала...

```text
R------>------:
        D     :
              :
G-------------:------- mono out
              :
      D D     :  D= 1N914 diode
B------>->----:     or similar

                 --->---
                 -     +
                    (marked end)
```

Следующая проблема заключается в том, что компьютер выдаёт совмещённую строчную и кадровую синхронизацию (H & V), тогда как монитор требует их раздельно. В зависимости от внутренней схемы входов синхронизации монитора, он может заработать, если просто соединить их вместе и подключить к выходу синхронизации Spectrum. Однако может потребоваться резистор или диод последовательно с одним из них или с обоими, чтобы добиться нужного результата.

Я предполагаю, что «зарезервированные» контакты либо используются для сообщения ПК, какой тип монитора подключён, либо относятся к выводам для дополнительных сигналов (то есть RGB для цветных мониторов).

Хотя лично для себя я с высокой вероятностью мог бы добиться удовлетворительного результата методом проб и ошибок, советовать это другим рискованно. Если методом проб я совершу ошибку и спалю собственный компьютер или монитор — это моя личная вина. Предлагать непроверенные идеи другим, рискуя повредить их технику, — совсем другое дело.
